functionalCorrectness.rationale: Build green, all 55 tests pass, lint+typecheck+vitest zero warnings, 12-symbol export surface verified on both ESM and CJS bundles, dist/index.d.ts has zero dicer references (T-071). Pack manifest exactly the spec'd 4 entries. Stubs are explicitly thrown (parseMultipartRelated) / rejected (fetchAndHandleMultipart) with deterministic 'not yet implemented (Sprint N)' messages — no silent successes. Zero critical bugs; the only nits are documentation-level (see codeQuality).

codeQuality.rationale: Zero `any`/`as never`/`as any` casts in src/; zero silent catches in src/; every error class extends Error and sets `name` to its literal class name. Logger uses event-style `{ level, msg, meta? }` shape per FR-018/JC-2; defaultLogger correctly re-shapes to positional console.warn(msg, meta). extractBoundary is genuinely a hand-written O(n) charCode-based tokenizer — verified line-by-line at src/extract-boundary.ts:66-201; no regex with backtracking risk. Imports are sorted (simple-import-sort), kebab-case file names, type imports use `import type`, .js extensions on imports. Standards/coding.md and standards/error-handling.md cleanly satisfied across src/. Minor nits: (a) tests/unit/extract-boundary.test.ts:113-117 has a `try/catch {}` with comment-only body inside the perf-gate test (technically a silent catch under standards/error-handling.md, but it's inside a timing-only test where catching swallowing is intentional, and ESLint's `no-empty: { allowEmptyCatch: false }` does not flag it because of the comment); (b) src/fetch-and-handle-multipart.ts:34 JSDoc says '@throws Sprint 1 stub: throws synchronously' but the body returns Promise.reject — wording mismatch only, no behavioral defect (test asserts `rejects.toThrow`).

specAdherence.rationale: Public re-exports in src/index.ts:9-30 match spec/api.md §Module entry exactly — same 5 functions, 7 error classes, 7 type aliases, no extras, no submodule exports. Hand-written dicer shim follows FR-DR-A-027 (only the surface used; exposes both `export default` and `export =` for the FR-DR-A-028 normalization to typecheck under both ESM and CJS bundles). FR-DR-A-028 normalization shape at src/parse-multipart-related.ts:50-51 matches the planner's mandated form verbatim. Error classes' structured properties match spec/api.md §5 (idleTimeoutMs, totalTimeoutMs, reason, bytesReceived, {maxPartBytes,partIndex,bytesReceived}, {limit,partIndex,cap,observed}, {maxParts,observed}). Logger type is `(event: { level: 'warn'; msg: string; meta?: unknown }) => void` exactly per JC-2.

Every FR allocated to Sprint 1 (FR-015..FR-020, FR-DR-A-027, FR-DR-A-028, FR-DR-D-001, FR-DR-D-004) has implementing code AND a real test. Stubs are clearly marked: parseMultipartRelated and fetchAndHandleMultipart contain verbose comments referencing the future sprint (2 / 5) plus deterministic throw/reject sentinels and dedicated stub-marker tests in tests/integration/sprint-1-stubs.test.ts. designQuality.rationale: Not applicable — this is a Node library project with no UI surface.

minorIssues.description: JSDoc @throws line says 'throws synchronously with Error(...)' but the implementation returns Promise.reject (so the rejection is async, not a sync throw). The integration test correctly uses `rejects.toThrow`. Wording-only; no behavioral impact. Recommend Sprint 5 update the doc string when the body is filled in.

T-080 perf gate's loop wraps `extractBoundary(pathological)` in `try { ... } catch { /* comment */ }` — technically a silent-catch-with-comment, allowed by ESLint's `no-empty: { allowEmptyCatch: false }` because the body is non-empty (has a comment), but standards/error-handling.md's intent is broader. The catch is semantically defensible (the assertion is timing, not value) but the planner could request that the helper be replaced with `expect.unreachable`/throw inside the try and assert the test wall time even if extractBoundary throws.

Inside `declare module 'dicer'`, both `export default Dicer;` AND `export = Dicer;` appear together. TypeScript permits this in declaration-merging contexts and `pnpm typecheck` passes — but it's an unusual shape that may surprise future maintainers. Worth a comment justifying both forms (one already exists at lines 69-74).
